Write an email to a colleague about a visit you are planning. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Plans for my visit to the Harlan Street office

Dear Margaret,

I have been meaning to write you for a week, but the days got away from me, so here it is at last. I am planning to come up to the Harlan Street office the second week of November, and I hope the time will suit you. I would arrive Tuesday morning, if the early train is running on schedule, and stay through Thursday afternoon.

The main reason for the trip is the new filing system. You have been using it for two months now, and I have heard a good deal about it, some of it kind and some of it not. Mr. Pruitt tells me it is "a fine idea for somebody with more patience than he has," which I take to mean it works well enough but he has not yet made peace with it. I would rather see it for myself than rely on hearsay. If you could spare an hour on Tuesday to walk me through a regular day's work, I would be much obliged.

Wednesday I would like to spend with the two new clerks. I know they are still finding their feet, and I don't want them to feel inspected, so I thought I might simply sit with each of them for the morning and let them go about their business. They will tell me more over a cup of tea than they ever would across a desk. If there is a quiet corner where I can set myself down without being in anybody's way, that is all I need.

Thursday morning I should like to go over the quarterly figures with you and Mr. Dalton. I have looked at the summary you sent, and there are two or three items I can't quite make out, particularly the freight charges, which seem to have jumped without any reason I can find. I dare say there is a perfectly good explanation, and I would rather hear it from you than guess at it.

As for lodging, please don't trouble yourself. I will take a room at the Alder House, as I did last spring. The beds are hard but the landlady is very obliging, and it is only a short walk from the office. I would be glad, however, if you would let me take you and Mr. Dalton to supper on Wednesday evening. There is a little place near the square that I have heard well spoken of, and I think we have earned a decent meal.

Will you let me know whether these days are convenient? If anything is going on that week which would make my coming a burden, say so plainly and I will change my plans without any hard feelings. I would rather arrive when I am welcome than when I am not.

With kind regards to you and the family,

[name]
